questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.**

How foolish I was to have believe that young woman!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: '**to have believe**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error lies in the verb form.
 
• The verb "**believe**" should be in the past participle form "**believed**" when used after "**to have**."
 
• The construction "**to have believed**" indicates the completion of the action of believing in the past.
 
• In contrast, "**to have believe**" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *How foolish I was to have believed that young woman!*

questions.question:

She is found to pass __derogatory__ remarks to others.

questions.question: **Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.**
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hapily** is incorrectly spelled.

• **Example**: *She finished her project ahead of schedule and happily celebrated her success with friends and family.*

• '**Slowly**' is an adverb derived from the adjective 'slow' by adding 'ly' at the end. It means at a slow pace or with reduced speed. (धीमी गति से)

questions.question:

Hypocrisy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Trickery". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypocrisy** is the practice of professing beliefs, feelings, or moral values that one does not hold or possess.
 
• It is insincerity by virtue of pretending to have qualities or beliefs that you do not really have.
 
 
• **Example: **"He called out the **hypocrisy **of politicians who claim to care about the environment but then vote against legislation protecting it."
 
 
 
• **Trickery **involves deception, fraud, or misrepresentation, often used to cheat or fool someone.
 
 
• **Example:** "The salesman relied on **trickery **to sell the faulty car, concealing its numerous mechanical problems from the buyer."
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Honesty:** Honesty involves truthfulness, straightforwardness, and lack of deceit, which contradicts the behavior of feigning or pretension embodied in hypocrisy.
 
• **Inaccuracy: **This term generally refers to the state of being incorrect or not precise, mostly in relation to facts, measurements, or predictions.
 
• **Sincerity: **Sincerity indicates genuineness, truthfulness, and a free expression of one's own feelings and beliefs, contrasting hypocritical pretense or deceit.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

His wife has a bad __habit for accusing him__ for others' mistakes too.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** habit of accusing him**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct preposition to use after "**habit**" is "**of**."
 
• We talk about having a habit of doing something, not a habit for doing something.
 
 
• **For example**, "*a habit of reading*," "*a habit of exercising*."
 
 
 
• The correct structure is "**accusing him of**."
 
• When we accuse someone, we use "**of**" to indicate the offense or wrongdoing.
 
 
• **For example**, "*accusing him of stealing*," "*accusing her of lying*."
 
 
 
• So, the **corrected sentence** is: "*His wife has a bad habit of accusing him of others' mistakes too.*"
 
• This version maintains proper prepositions and accurately conveys that the wife has a habit of accusing her husband of mistakes that others have made.

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.
